exam: A 45‑year‑old diabetic presents with oedema and hypertension. What is the first drug you would add? — ACEI/ARB to reduce proteinuria and protect kidneys.
A patient with DKD has serum potassium 5.8 mmol/L. What is the next step? — Hold ACEI/ARB, give a loop diuretic, and re‑check potassium.
A diabetic patient develops sudden rise in creatinine. What complication should you rule out? — Acute tubular necrosis from malaria or sepsis.
Which infection common in East Africa can accelerate DKD? — HIV or tuberculosis.
A patient with DKD is on an ACEI but develops cough. What is the likely cause? — ACEI‑induced cough; consider switching to ARB.
ai.title: Diabetic Kidney Disease
ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: Diabetic kidney disease is a progressive renal complication of diabetes, identified by albuminuria and declining eGFR. Early detection and ACEI/ARB therapy slow progression, while management of blood pressure, glycaemia and comorbidities is essential.

t.b: Assesses glomerular filtration; decline indicates progression
Rules out infection or other proteinuria causes

sections.p: KDIGO stages DKD by eGFR and albuminuria, guiding treatment intensity.

t.b: Combines eGFR and albuminuria to estimate progression risk

sections.p: Primary driver is hyperglycaemia‑induced glomerular injury; secondary factors common in low‑resource settings include infections and herbal nephrotoxins.

t.b: Higher levels correlate with faster DKD progression

b: Anuria or oliguria in advanced disease
sections.p: Early DKD is asymptomatic. Later stages show oedema, hypertension, reduced urine output, and anaemia.
Use available tests to confirm DKD and rule out mimics.

t.b: Positive → DKD; negative → consider other causes

sections.p: DKD can rapidly progress to ESRD; complications include hyperkalaemia, volume overload, and cardiovascular events.
Treat underlying diabetes, control blood pressure with ACEI/ARB, and address comorbidities.

t.b: Avoid if serum potassium >5.5 or eGFR <30

sections.p: Regular monitoring of albuminuria, eGFR, BP, and glycaemia prevents progression.

t.b: Counselling on salt restriction and smoking cessation

sections.p: Other causes of proteinuria and CKD must be excluded.
